title: Flimsy Wire
text:
Flimsy Wire. Up to this point, my main method for slicing blocks of cheese has been a large, stainless steel chef’s knife. It does the job but it’s also a bit awkward and admittedly not ideal. I looked to this cheese slicer as a possible replacement. I would politely describe my experience with it as “disappointing”.

This is a guillotine-style slicer – it has a handle with a thin steel wire that is used to cut through the block when the handle is pressed down, making a clean, straight cut. The surface on which the cheese sits is a nice marble slab with a groove cut in it so that the wire can pass completely through the block without leaving an uncut lip.

In theory this works, and I have seen it work well in other similar slicers. However, for this particular slicer the wire is so flimsy and weak that it bends when slicing and I believe it’s a matter of time (not very long) before it breaks and I have to restring it.

I can’t recommend this slicer. I’ve gone back to using my chef’s knife while I search for better wire to replace the wire that came in this slicer. There are less expensive options that work better.
